experiment: DFlash2 sidecar drafter on dense Qwen3.8-27B
context: first DFlash2 sidecar ever served on this card; ngl forced to 40 (vs 48 without sidecar) to make VRAM room for the drafter

finding: DFlash2's published acceptance claims are TRUE and if anything conservative: 0.737/0.519 with mean accepted length 3.93/3.08 — the best drafter acceptance ever measured on this card. But the NET decode (4.02/3.28 tok/s) loses to the embedded-MTP d2 baseline (4.63-5.3) because the sidecar's ~1.1 GB VRAM forces 8 main layers onto the CPU band (measured slope from our ngl sweeps: ~18% penalty).
conclusion: on 8 GB cards the DFlash2 family is VRAM-disqualified vs embedded MTP: acceptance quality cannot pay for the offload demotion. On 12 GB+ cards (3060 class, per the upstream cards' own target market) the drafter rides free and would win. Park again with this measured evidence.
family: andrew-paul Q2_K/Q3_K_M imatrix-calibrated variants untested (only andrew-paul's Q2_K saves ~400 MB vs Q8/Q4 — insufficient to recover 8 layers; no path to a win on 8 GB observed
